test_policy.notes: ACT or SAT is not required. Applicants can be admitted with any one of: ACT 18 (SAT 960), a high school GPA of 2.6, or top 60% of the graduating class (the international page prints SAT 970 instead of 960). The international page lists SAT/ACT among the tests that can be sent in place of an English test. Some scholarships (WolfPACT) use ACT/SAT scores but also have a no-score track.

requirements.notes: International degree-seeking first-year file: online application with $25 non-refundable fee, high school transcript/marks sheet (certified English translation if needed; mailed official transcripts required upon admission), one test score (English test or SAT/ACT), passport page, Declaration of Finances form with bank statement, immunization form. Essay and recommendations are not listed. The IPEDS undergraduate application fee for 2024-25 was $20. After admission the student gets an I-20 and F-1 visa instructions.

deadlines.label: International application (fall 2027 entry): no deadline published
deadlines.notes: Neither the international students page nor the undergraduate requirements page prints an application deadline or a decision timeline. Apply early enough to get an I-20 and an F-1 visa appointment before the semester.

deadlines.label: WolfPACT scholarship priority deadline (first-year, fall 2027)
deadlines.notes: The page prints 'Priority deadline: March 1' without a year; taken as March 1, 2027. No separate application: send the admission application, fee, high school transcript and ACT/SAT scores (scores optional for the no-score track) for an official award notice.

english_policy.waiver_notes: The international page asks for one of: TOEFL iBT, IELTS, Duolingo, SAT 970+ or ACT 18+, so a qualifying SAT/ACT can stand in for an English test. The factsheet (titled 2023/2024) says the English score is not required for applicants from English-speaking countries; the current page names no country list. No ESL or conditional-admission pathway is mentioned on the pages read. Nursing (BSN) sets higher English minimums for non-native speakers.

english.notes: The page prints 'TOEFL IBT (61-70 or above)'; the exact threshold inside that range is not stated, and 61 is the lowest figure printed (the factsheet says 61 or higher). Nursing BSN: 84 with Speaking 26 (exams before 2026-01-21); for exams on/after 2026-01-21 on the 1-6 scale, 4.5 overall with Speaking 5.0. The general-program minimum on the 1-6 scale is not published. Institution code 6487 per the page.
Nursing BSN: 6.5 overall with at least 6.0 in each module.

aid.notes: The WolfPACT merit scholarship (4-year totals from $4,000 for a 3.00-3.49 GPA with no/low test score, up to $16,000 for a 3.75+ GPA with ACT 28+/SAT 1300+; 3.0 GPA to renew) needs no separate application. The current WolfPACT page says 'all first-year students' without naming international students; the factsheet (titled 2023/2024) says WolfPACT is available to international degree-seekers and points to patrick.woods@northern.edu for other awards. Whether international students can receive need-based aid is not stated on the pages read.

cost.notes: 2026-27 yearly estimates for 30 credit hours: tuition and fees combined $10,077 resident (includes new freshmen from the listed South Dakota Advantage states) and $12,379 out-of-state; housing $6,300 (average residence hall) plus food $4,974 (21 meals/week) = $11,274. The page does not say which rate international students pay, though the factsheet (titled 2023/2024) lists a $200 per-semester international student fee and ~$1,316 health insurance on top of tuition; current amounts are not confirmed. Out-of-state per-credit tuition is $376.40.

majors.notes: Apply to NSU as pre-nursing; most students apply to the BSN in sophomore year after prerequisites (min. college GPA 2.7). Direct admission for first-time freshmen with ACT 27+ and HS GPA 3.5+, or HS GPA 3.8+ (keep a 3.0 college GPA). Nursing application window is Aug 15-Sep 30 for fall. Non-native English speakers need TOEFL 84/IELTS 6.5/Duolingo 110 unless exempt. Seat limits are not published on the page.

sat.note: SAT school code per the international and undergraduate requirements pages.

act.note: NSU's pages give two different ACT codes (3916 on the requirements page, 3169 on the international page); confirm with NSU before sending.

toefl.note: The international page prints school code 6487 next to TOEFL iBT.
